correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary slice, a near-norming set either contains an atom, yielding the normalized atomic witness with distance at least 1+||f||_1-2m(f), or has an atomless positive-measure part, where sigma-finiteness and nonatomic divisibility give finite sets with arbitrarily small f-mass and distances approaching 1+||f||_1. Conversely, a slice supported on an atom carrying mass p gives delta c(f) <= 1+||f||_1-2p; taking p upward to the supremal atomic mass and using dc<=delta c closes equality. The m=0 case and nonattainment of m are handled by limits. The finite rational checker is only algebraic corroboration.
risks: The proof uses the real sigma-finite L1 dual identification and nonatomic divisibility exactly as stated; no complex or non-localizable extension was checked.
